name: Tooth-Colored Dental Fillings
teaser: Natural-looking restorations that blend seamlessly with your smile.
overview: When a cavity or minor tooth damage needs repair, a tooth-colored composite filling restores the tooth's structure and appearance in a single appointment. Unlike older amalgam (silver) fillings, composite fillings are matched to the shade of your natural tooth — making them virtually invisible.

The procedure is straightforward: the decay is removed, the area is cleaned, and the composite resin is bonded directly to the tooth. The result is a strong, comfortable restoration that looks and feels completely natural.

whatToExpect.title: Examination & Numbing
whatToExpect.body: We'll identify the affected area, discuss the restoration with you, and apply local anesthesia to keep you comfortable throughout.

whatToExpect.title: Decay Removal & Bonding
whatToExpect.body: The decayed portion of the tooth is gently removed, and the composite resin is carefully applied in layers and bonded to the tooth.

whatToExpect.title: Shaping & Polish
whatToExpect.body: The filling is shaped to match your natural bite, then polished for a smooth, natural finish — usually done in a single appointment.

faqs.question: How long do tooth-colored fillings last?
faqs.answer: Composite fillings typically last 7–15 years with proper care, though this varies based on the size of the filling, location, and individual habits.

faqs.question: Are tooth-colored fillings as strong as silver ones?
faqs.answer: Modern composite resin is very durable and suitable for most cavities. For very large restorations in high-pressure areas, your dentist will discuss the best material for your situation.

faqs.question: Will my tooth be sensitive after a filling?
faqs.answer: Some mild sensitivity to hot, cold, or pressure for a few days after a filling is normal. This usually resolves on its own. If sensitivity persists, let us know.
